newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac allay furor.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac allay furor.

text.p: Acting to assuage mounting congressional criticism, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac said on Thursday they would further explain several controversial programs to key lawmakers and regulators.
Earlier, House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach called for an inquiry into new programs at the two government-sponsored entities, heavyweights in the U.S. mortgage industry.
"We welcome the dialogue with chairman Leach and others," a spokesman for Fannie Mae said. Leach, Republican of Iowa, questioned the company's new mortgage insurance plan.
Leach also questioned Freddie Mac's investment policies, specifically a plan to invest in securities not related to mortgages.
"We will respond to any requests for information on our investment practices," a spokeswoman for the company said. "We firmly believe our investment strategies support our housing mission."
Last week, following criticism from Leach, Freddie Mac sold $340 million of Philip Morris corporate bonds.
Fannie Mae said it expects to proceed with its program to provide first time home buyers with mortgage insurance.
"We certainly plan to introduce this product once we have this dialogue with chairman Leach and our regulators," the spokesman said. "We don't see any charter issues but we're going to discuss this."
Fannie Mae officials went to Capitol Hill Thursday to brief legislators on the program, the spokesman added.

Under the program, Fannie Mae would purchase for first time homebuyers an insurance policy to cover mortgage payments in the event the borrower became unemployed or disabled during the first five years fo the loan. The policy would pay off the mortgage entirely if the borrower died.
Leach said the program might in effect allow Fannie Mae to make below-market rate loans to insurance companies.
He asked Housing and Community Development secretary Andrew Cuomo to review the program and Freddie Mac's non-mortgage investment activities.
A spokeswoman for Cuomo said the secretary's office had received the letter. "We are conducting appropriate reviews," the spokeswoman said.
